newsitem.title: USA: UAL pilots see arbiter's rule in April.
newsitem.headline: UAL pilots see arbiter's rule in April.

text.p: Pilots of UAL Corp's United Airlines said they expect an arbiter to rule on a mid-term wage proposal by late-April.
On Thursday, The Air Line Pilots Association overwhelmingly rejected a wage proposal that offered a 10 percent wage increase over four years.
A mid-term wage adjustment was included as a provision of the pilots' 1994 employee-ownership agreement (ESOP). The pilots rejected the offer by a four-to-one margin.
United and the pilots will now submit to binding arbitration, but an independent arbiter has not yet been assigned to the case, a spokesman for the pilots said Friday.
Under terms of the pilots' an arbiter can assign wage increases of up to five percent for 1997 and 1998.
Any wage hikes set by the arbiter must be in place by July 12, according to the ESOP contract, the union said.
